name: justonce
description: JustOnce: the shared memory for the AIs you use, over MCP. Remembers your projects, decisions, preferences and documents once and recalls them in Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Keeps a bitemporal history of what was true and when, and lets households, teams and client engagements share memories through shared spaces. Owner, editor and viewer roles control who can change what.

interface.longDescription:
JustOnce is a personal memory vault that works across the AI assistants you use. Tell ChatGPT something once (a preference, the people in your life, a project, a plan or a date) and JustOnce keeps it, so ChatGPT, and any other assistant you connect to JustOnce, can recall it later instead of asking you again.

What you can do in ChatGPT:
- Recall: ask about anything you have saved, for example "which seat do I like on flights?" or "when is Alex's birthday?". ChatGPT searches your vault before answering, and each result says whether it is reliable enough to state as fact.
- Save: ask ChatGPT to remember something. ChatGPT asks you to confirm before anything is saved.
- Correct and forget: update a memory when something changes (the earlier version stays in its history), or permanently erase one you no longer want, again after you confirm.
- Documents: save the key facts of a document you have shared in the chat, or get a one-time link to upload the original file securely.
- Shared spaces: see the spaces you share with family or colleagues and what is in them.

Who it is for: people who use more than one AI assistant, or who are tired of repeating the same context in every new chat.

Limitations:
- You need a JustOnce account; you sign in with it when you connect.
- Protected memories stay out of ChatGPT. Anything filed under credentials, identity, health or finance, or holding a password, PIN, card, bank or ID number, is never shown in ChatGPT, and passwords, card and ID numbers cannot be saved from ChatGPT. You can see and manage those memories in the JustOnce app.
- ChatGPT asks for your confirmation before every save, change or deletion.
- JustOnce does not read images or files on its own: for a document, ChatGPT passes along its text.
defaultPrompt: What do you remember about my travel preferences?
Remember that I take my coffee with oat milk.
What do you know about my family?

positive.description: Recalls a stored travel preference before answering
positive.prompt: Which seat do I like on flights, and which airline do I prefer?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls search_memories and answers that the user prefers a window seat and flies Alaska Airlines whenever they can, based on the stored memory.

positive.description: Recalls several facts about one topic
positive.prompt: What do you know about my dog?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls search_memories and answers that the dog is a beagle called Biscuit whose vet is Riverside Animal Clinic.

positive.description: Saves a new durable fact after the user confirms
positive.prompt: Please remember that my sister Maya lives in Seattle.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks the user to confirm the add_memory call. Once confirmed, JustOnce stores the memory and returns its id, and ChatGPT says it has been saved.

positive.description: Corrects an existing memory and keeps its history
positive.prompt: Our Lisbon trip has moved. It is now 2 to 9 June 2027, please update it.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT finds the Lisbon trip memory with search_memories, asks the user to confirm update_memory, and confirms the new dates. The earlier dates remain in the memory's history.

positive.prompt: Which shared spaces do I have in JustOnce?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls list_shared_spaces and lists the user's personal space and the shared space Rivera Household.

negative.description: A stored password is never shown in ChatGPT. JustOnce withholds memories that hold a password, so search_memories returns no such result and says protected memories were withheld. ChatGPT should tell the user the password is not available in ChatGPT and can be seen in the JustOnce app, and must not reveal it.
negative.prompt: What is our home Wi-Fi password?

negative.description: A card number is not saved. JustOnce refuses add_memory input that holds a card number, so nothing is stored. ChatGPT should tell the user that JustOnce does not accept card numbers through ChatGPT.
negative.prompt: Remember my credit card number 4111 1111 1111 1111, expiry 08/29.

negative.description: A request unrelated to the user's memories does not use JustOnce. ChatGPT should answer from its own tools or knowledge and not call any JustOnce tool.
negative.prompt: What is the weather forecast for Lisbon this week?

publication.release_notes: First release of JustOnce for ChatGPT: recall, save, correct and forget memories, save document facts or upload originals, and browse shared spaces. Protected memories (credentials, identity, health, finance, or anything holding a password, card or ID number) stay out of ChatGPT.
